subject: GCP/Azure marketplace bundle: SKU catalog, metering, and reseller margin mechanics
messages:
From: Kevin Zhang <kevin@cloudops.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudops.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 14:03:12 -0800
Subject: Evaluating a cross-cloud private offer (GCP + Azure) and channel passback questions

Camila —

Thanks again for the demo last week. CloudOps is evaluating a two-cloud private offer that covers both GCP and Azure marketplace delivery for our enterprise customers. A couple of things we need clarity on before we take this to procurement:

- Can Redwood publish a single private offer that maps to separate SKUs on GCP and Azure while preserving a single list price for our quoting tool?
- How does the channel passback flow work when we have a reseller on Azure but direct listing in GCP? We need to understand net vs list and whether passbacks are computed pre-tax and pre-discount.
- We're sensitive to metering buckets — we would prefer per-1M-token metering on GCP and per-hour-node on Azure in the same commitment. Is that supported or does Redwood require a unified metering surface?

Attaching a short requirements doc with the use cases and expected volumes. Can you point me to a sketch of how you’ve handled cross-marketplace bundles before? If this looks feasible, procurement will ask for an illustrative price schedule and expected channel margin for our reseller partner (they typically require a 12–18% net passback).

Best,
Kevin
Director, Cloud Procurement
CloudOps Inc

Attachment: cloudops_requirements.pdf (1 page — bundle scope + expected volumes)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Zhang <kevin@cloudops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Nov 2027 09:18:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluating a cross-cloud private offer (GCP + Azure) and channel passback questions

Kevin —

Thanks for the note and the requirements doc — very helpful. Short answers up front:

- Yes, we can surface a single commercial quote while mapping to discrete marketplace SKUs. That is a common pattern for customers who want a single PoR (purchase order) but need marketplace delivery.
- Channel passback can be configured per-transaction to either apply against list or against net price; we will need to choose one approach for the committed pricing schedule.
- Metering differences are handled via our routing and aggregation layer; you can have different metering surfaces per cloud as long as the commitment reconcilers are aligned on a single consumption unit for the commitment (we often convert to token-equivalent units for mixed-meter deals).

I've looped in Ben and Laura from pricing/finance — they’ll draft an example schedule and suggested passback split for your reseller. Marcus Lin from engineering will help confirm any SKU/technical constraints for GCP + Azure mapping.

Can we schedule a 30-min call early next week to walk through a first draft? I’ll send a proposed MAP (mutual action plan) and an illustrative pricing sketch beforehand.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Head of Strategic GTM, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai

---
Camila Reyes
Head of Strategic GTM | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Nov 2027 10:42:27 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluating a cross-cloud private offer (GCP + Azure) and channel passback questions

Camila —

I pulled together a quick pass at the economics and an approach called out below. See attached workbook for line-item math (proposed-passback.xlsx). Key items:

1) Packaging approach
- Create a single commercial bundle (Bundle-A) with three internal SKUs: GCP-runtime, Azure-runtime, and Support. The bundle price is what CloudOps will see on the quote; marketplace SKUs represent delivery.

2) Metering reconciliation
- We'll normalize to a token-equivalent unit for the commitment baseline. GCP token-metered usage maps 1:1; Azure hourly nodes are converted via a conversion factor derived from sample tests (we used 1 node-hour ≈ 120k tokens for sizing).

3) Channel passback mechanics
- Proposed default: compute passback on net price (post-customer discount) but pre-tax. Reason: gives reseller predictable margin irrespective of list anchoring strategies.
- Suggested reseller net passback: 14% of net revenue (in the middle of CloudOps target range).

4) Discount cadence and list vs net
- We recommend publishing a list price and offering a 10% commitment discount for Year 1; any additional promotional discounts should be applied outside the committed schedule and should not change the passback basis.

5) Accounting & Marketplace constraints
- GCP and Azure have different invoice flows; we’ll instrument reconciliation hooks so we can attribute consumption to the right marketplace SKU for billing and audit. There will be a small operational uplift for mapping for the first 90 days.

If that direction looks OK, I’ll refine the numbers for the MAP and add examples of how the passback would affect the reseller payout across a range of gross-to-net scenarios.

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-passback.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 tabs)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Zhang <kevin@cloudops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Nov 2027 09:02:44 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluating a cross-cloud private offer (GCP + Azure) and channel passback questions

Kevin —

Thanks — attaching a short MAP and an illustrative price schedule to make this concrete. High-level summary (see attachments and Drive link for the worked example):

- Proposed commercial: Bundle-A list price $120,000 / mo (1M-token-equivalent unit). Year 1 commitment discount: 10% (net $108,000).
- Reseller passback: 14% of net revenue (monthly remittance).
- Metering: GCP token-metered units + Azure node-hours normalized to token-equivalent for commit consumption; individual marketplace invoices will still contain marketplace SKUs for legal/fulfillment reasons.
- Implementation timeline: SKU catalog mapping and reconciliation hooks — 4 weeks; marketplace listing sync and QA — additional 2 weeks.

Next steps I propose:
- 30-min call next Tue (Nov 16) to confirm conversion factor and the passback basis.
- You to share reseller contract (if any) so we can map overlap with your terms.
- Once we align on the schedule, Redwood will generate a draft private offer (DocuSign link) and a marketplace manifest for each cloud.

Quote from Ben’s analysis: "Compute passback on net price (post-commit discount, pre-tax) to give reseller a stable margin signal across promotions."

Attachments: MAP_CloudOps_bundle_v1.pdf, illustrative-pricing.csv (in Drive)

—
Camila Reyes
Head of Strategic GTM | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai

Camila / team —

This layout is very helpful — thank you. A couple follow-ups from procurement and our reseller partner:

1) Can you confirm whether the reseller passback of 14% will be paid monthly or quarterly? Our reseller prefers monthly remittance to align with their cash flow.
2) For the metering conversion you mentioned (1 node-hour ≈ 120k tokens), can you provide the test log or the microbench data Ben referenced so our platform team can validate?
3) We need to understand if list price must be equal across marketplaces for certification reasons; if not, will differing list prices affect reseller commission calculations on their end?

Subject to the answers, procurement is ready to move to signature. I’ve attached our standard procurement form — please indicate if any sections will need legal redlines. We would also appreciate a short DocuSign draft of the private offer once the final price schedule is confirmed.

Thanks,
Kevin
Procurement
CloudOps Inc
